what: Sommelier V1+ P8: free quality measurement and performance benchmarks of the integrated build after the end-review fixes (commit 85bd32f: one cellar index per question for the check via prepareAnswerCheck, the serving-facts lookup, the menu parser, the quantity arithmetic and the annotation/quantity copy). First measured on 0fc8c09 (see beforeReviewFixes). No model was called, nothing was sent, no key was used; the v1-ai engine was not run.
machine: 4 shared cores (Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz), Node 22; other agents were running on the same machine (load average 4.7 at the start of the latency run, 3.3 at its end; 512 s). Wall-clock numbers are this machine on this day, not production.

latency.how: createSommelierService as server/services.ts wires it, a fake model that answers at once with a fixed realistic answer (3 bottle_refs for a pairing, one course entry per course for a menu when the schema asks for courses, the named wine for a serving question), in-memory reads, generated cellars (bench-cellar.ts). Per cell: 20 warm-up rounds, then 200 measured rounds, every configuration once per round in a rotating order. p50/p95/max of the wall clock of one ask; delta = configuration minus V1 (or minus V1 without a model) in the same cell. Percentile as score.ts: the value at floor(p*n).

questions.pairing-guests: We are 6 for dinner tonight: roast lamb with rosemary and garlic. Which bottle should I open? (a pairing with a guest count, so quantities has work)
questions.menu-3: Oysters to start, then roast lamb, and for dessert chocolate fondant. Which wine with each course?
questions.serving: How should I serve the Vajrelli, and should I decant it? (names one cellar wine by its producer)

summary.whereTheTimeGoes: With one cellar index per question (prepareAnswerCheck, p50 11.5 ms at 3,000 wines) each check of a text costs p50 0.2 ms, so a menu's course reasons no longer pay the index again (checkAnswerClaims, index and check at once: p50 10.7 ms at 3,000 wines, was 176). The serving facts' lookup of the named wine is p50 0.7 ms at 3,000 wines (was 90). See `components`.
summary.profileReadsPerAsk: at most 1 with annotate (or with the fallback on the no-model path), 0 otherwise: measured, not assumed. In-memory here; in production one round trip to vintage_insights.
summary.noModelPath: V1 without a model: p95 up to 210 ms at 3,000 wines (the plain pairing engine). With fallback: within +4.3 ms of it in every cell.

beforeReviewFixes.what: The latency the first P8 run measured on 0fc8c09, before the end-review fixes, kept for comparison (p95 delta to V1, ms).
beforeReviewFixes.verdict: +300 ms proposal not met for all five together at 3,000 wines (4 of 6 cells); met everywhere else.

cost.how: The request the service builds for one ask, recorded before the fake model answers. promptChars = system + user + JSON schema (as paid.ts estimating() counts). inputTokens = ceil(chars/3). maxOutputTokens after planCall. highMicro = pricing.ts estimateCost (input + full output allowance, two attempts). reservationMicro = paid.ts reservationFor. typicalMicro = one attempt, input + a typical output (180 tokens, +45 per course for a planned menu; an assumption, not measured). vsV1 = percent change against V1 (prompt v6, no part) for the same question, conversation and cellar. The cellar list is capped at 120 wines (DIGEST_MAX), so 120 and 3000 wines give nearly the same prompt.

evalSets.how: Every scenario V1 can attempt (needs within pairing, facts) asked turn by turn through the service with the parts on and paid.ts estimating() as the model; the V1 row equals the repo's own `pnpm sommelier:eval --engine v1-ai --estimate --set main --needs pairing,facts` (131 calls, 340,592 tokens in, $0.2031).

fallback.result: Reproduced exactly on 85bd32f (as before on 0fc8c09): every per-scenario vector of v1-fallback and v1-basic equals the committed p7 vectors (main 146 and 124, holdout-dev 45 and 45; holdout-test 43 and 43 compared under the same salt, reported in totals only), and every difference and 95% interval equals p7-fallback.json to 4 decimals. fallback.test.ts passes.
fallback.note: The v1-fallback engine calls createSommelierFallback directly and then the service with llm = null; it does not go through the service's own fallback wiring (deps.parts + deps.fallback). fallback-wired.ts plays every scenario both ways (the engine's way, and the integrated service with parts = fallback and deps.fallback set, llm = null): on 85bd32f the last answers are identical for main 246/246, holdout-dev 45/45 and holdout-test 43/43 (totals only). Tested in bench.test.ts.

annotationSample.command: pnpm --filter @cellr/sommelier-eval run annotation-sample --write, then pnpm prettier --write on the file
annotationSample.note: NOT reviewed by any person. Regenerated on 85bd32f with the new copy (e.g. 'from its profile', 'not reserved', 'decant gently off the sediment shortly before serving'). 49 of 50 rows carry a lowest-confidence flag from the code itself (serving by rule of thumb for the style or the colour, or a window estimated for the style); one row (a wine with a researched profile) is stated as from its profile.

menu.scorer: menu-score.ts scoreMenu/scoreCourse: per course right / acceptable / poor against menuExpectations (the dish cards' AI-written labels). Tested on synthetic answers and end to end through the service with a model that picks the labelled right wines (18/18 menus, every course right) and one that picks poor wines.
menu.estimateNote: One call per turn (18 menus, 21 turns). Nothing was sent: paid.ts estimating() answers 'unavailable' and the service gives its plain answer, so the follow-up turns carry '…' as the earlier answer; a paid run would carry the model's words (up to 400 characters each in the history), about 3 x 400 characters more in all.

gate.note: Thresholds are the closeout's proposals (D-50), not owner decisions. 'Free' means without a model.
gate.firstBottleRight_noPoorBottle_usefulAnsw: NOT MEASURABLE FREE: needs the paid v1-ai baseline and V1+ run (owner's budget approval, D-51).
gate.inventedBottleVintageFact: Not measurable free for answers with a model. Free paths: v1-fallback invents 0 bottles on all three sets (fallback.test.ts); the fake-model harness cannot test it (the fake is well-behaved).
gate.unverifiedPriceShopStock: Not measurable free for answers with a model. Free path: v1-fallback gives no buying advice or price on all three sets.
gate.annotationCorrectness: Fixtures: the repo's unit tests pass (pnpm test). Sample of 50: REGENERATED on 85bd32f with the new copy, NOT REVIEWED (results/p4-annotation-sample.md). NOT MET until a person reviews it.
gate.latency: Part overhead only (fake model, in-memory reads). MET in every cell measured: every part alone and all five together, at 25, 120, 500 and 3,000 wines, 1 and 12 messages (worst +35.9 ms: all five, 3-course menu, 3,000 wines; before the review fixes +891.6 ms). The real p95 with a model must still be measured in the paid run.
gate.cost: Prompt and output allowance, free estimate. MET for every non-menu question: high estimate +1.1 to +6.9% (all parts; worst a serving question at 25 wines); prompt characters up to +17.1% there (the serving block is longer since the review fixes; +7.3% at 120 wines), so on characters alone a serving question in a small cellar is above +10%, on the cost estimate it is not. On the eval sets main / holdout-dev / holdout-test: +2.3 / +2.4 / +2.4% high estimate (+5.5 to +6.1% characters), check being the only part that changes their prompts. NOT MET on a worst-case basis for a NEW MENU: the output allowance grows 70 tokens a course (900 -> 1110 for 3 courses, 1460 for 8), so the high estimate is +12.8% (3 courses) and +28.2% (8 courses) with menu alone at 120 wines, +43.3% / +45.7% (menu / all) for 8 courses at 25 wines; the input alone is +6 to +9% at 120 wines but +14 to +21% at 25 wines. Over the 18-menu set: +17.2% high estimate (+13.6% prompt characters) with menu on, +19.6% (+19.6%) with check and menu. Unchanged by the review fixes except the serving and comparison rows.
gate.fallbackVsPlain: Reproduced on 85bd32f (identical to 0fc8c09 and to P7): MET on main and holdout-test (lower bounds +24 / +14 first bottle, +51 / +35 no poor bottle); holdout-dev first bottle lower bound +0, NOT STRICTLY MET (as in P7).

limitations: Fake model: answers at once with a fixed, well-formed answer that follows the prompt (refs as [[ref]] under v7). Real models take seconds, write other words (which changes what check does and how long it takes) and sometimes fail; the measured numbers are the overhead of the app's own code only.
In-memory reads: the cellar, profiles, taste and Tonight reads cost nothing here. The parts add at most one profiles read per ask (measured); its database round trip is not in the numbers.

Shared CPU: 4 cores shared with other agents (load average 4.7 at the start of the latency run, 3.3 at its end). Configurations were interleaved round by round so a slow moment falls on all; absolute times are this machine on this day.

Generated cellars: realistic in shape but invented (bench-cellar.ts); real cellars differ in names, which changes the cost of the name-matching rules. The eval's own fixture ids are counted (refs 32 characters instead of 6), so the eval-set cost estimates err high in absolute terms for every configuration alike; the bench cellars use random-looking ids.

Cost is an estimate: characters/3 as tokens and the full output allowance (pricing.ts estimateCost); the typical-output column assumes 180 tokens (+45 a course), not measured. No provider bill was read.

AI-written labels: the dish cards behind the eval sets and the menu set were written by an AI and reviewed by nobody who knows wine (R-01, R-11). The fallback numbers and the menu scorer inherit that.
The menu estimate's follow-up turns carry '…' as the earlier answer (nothing was sent), up to about 1,200 history characters less than a paid run.
The annotation sample has not been reviewed by a person; its flags are the code's own bases, not a judgement.

In the serving question the wine is named by its producer only ('the Vajrelli'): with 'the Vajrelli Barolo' the serving facts still give no block in the 120- and 3,000-wine cellars on 85bd32f (more than three wines match by name, FACTS_WINES_MAX), as P4-P5 documents.
